_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: James Legge (1815-1897). The Chinese classics: the Tao Teh King (Sacred Books of the East 39, 1891), the Analects (Chinese Classics I, 1861/1893), and Faxian's Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms (1886); since round 64 also his other Sacred Books of the East volumes: the Shu King, Shih King and Hsiao King (SBE 3, 2nd ed. 1899), the Yi King (SBE 16, 1882), the Li Ki (SBE 27-28, 1885) and the Kwang-ze with the Thai-Shang Tractate (SBE 39-40, 1891), raw OCR of the Clarendon printings. PD. Added 2026-10-02/03 by lane C (round 5) under the coordinator's standing instruction to choose further translator shelves; Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted in the relay burst.

legge-tao-teh-king: The Tao Teh King, or the Tao and its Characteristics

legge-shu-king: Sacred Books of the East vol. 3: The Shu King, the Religious Portions of the Shih King, the Hsiao King (Clarendon Press, 2nd ed., 1899)
legge-yi-king: Sacred Books of the East vol. 16: The Yi King (Clarendon Press, 1882)
legge-li-ki-1: Sacred Books of the East vol. 27: The Li Ki, books I-X (Clarendon Press, 1885)
legge-li-ki-2: Sacred Books of the East vol. 28: The Li Ki, books XI-XLVI (Clarendon Press, 1885)
legge-kwang-ze-1: Sacred Books of the East vol. 39: The Writings of Kwang-ze, books I-XVII (from The Texts of Taoism, part I) (Clarendon Press, 1891)
legge-kwang-ze-2: Sacred Books of the East vol. 40: The Texts of Taoism, part II (Clarendon Press, 1891)

A Million Books Project copy (sacredbooksofthe003275mbp) was tried first and dropped: its library slip says 'pages missing in the book'.

legge-kwang-ze-1.note: Cut from vol. 39 where the Kwang-ze section begins (its introduction of brief notices, then books I-XVII): the volume's Tao Teh King, with the general introduction to Taoism that precedes it, is left behind because the Tao Teh King is already on this shelf from Gutenberg 216. H. A. Giles's Chuang Tzu (giles shelf) is a different translation.

_excluded.pg-3100-4094: Gutenberg 3100 and 4094 are the Chinese-language text of the Chinese Classics, not the translation.

_name_words_note: Translator name(s) only: fetch_shelf.py treats these as the identity check (one must appear in the fetched text), so the original author's name is deliberately NOT listed.
_verified_note: Evidence that each source's rights/identity line was read (lane C review fix, 2026-10-02, pipeline run over the fetched files; no book text recorded). PG: the header's Translator: line and the COPYRIGHTED marker. IA: whether the translator's name appears in the first 30 KB of OCR, and the years printed in the first 15 KB of front matter (scanner/digitizer lines skipped). Any post-1930 year there was examined by eye; see the title's scan_edition.

legge-li-ki-1.author: The title page OCR reads 'TRANSLATED BY JAMES LEGGt ... PART III THE Li Ki, I-X' for James Legge, under the Clarendon Press 1885 imprint. Checked by eye 2026-10-17.
